summary.headline: KSH International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 108% YoY to INR1,164 crore; EBITDA per ton hit ~INR93,000, with management guiding to a sustainable ~INR75,000.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,164 crore (+108% YoY) and EBITDA was INR74.4 crore (vs INR40.3 crore a year ago and INR56.3 crore in Q4), with a record quarterly PAT of INR42.2 crore. Management attributed the strong EBITDA per ton mainly to a record CTC contribution, higher exports and new OEM customers priced at market-linked value-addition rates, with a weaker rupee also helping. Phase 1 of the Supa expansion is complete, with 14,400 MT of the 30,000 MT phase 2 added so far and full 59,000 MT installed capacity targeted by March 2027. Management signed a five-year framework agreement with Hitachi Energy, though quantity and price are not yet defined.

segments.name: Specialized wires (CTC, T&D focus)
segments.commentary: Revenue +113% YoY to a record share of total revenue, driven by CTC and exports; management expects the mix to normalise over the next two to three quarters as standard-wire capacity comes in. CTC is 50-75% of the specialized segment, and 765 kV/HVDC is ~25% of CTC volume.

segments.name: Standard wires (EV, AC compressors, motors, DG alternators)
segments.commentary: Revenue +83% YoY; EBITDA per ton improved marginally as utilisation of round-wire capacity rose. Management expects standard-wire contribution to rise in the second half of FY27.

segments.name: Upcast copper scrap recycling (Chakan)
segments.commentary: 5,000 MT facility commissioned in the last week of Q1 to recycle in-house copper scrap, investment ~INR6-7 crore. CFO expects only a few rupees of benefit to gross profit in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA per ton of ~INR75,000 for FY27, dependent on product mix, exports and currency; management said this is not a formal guidance figure.
Fixed costs expected to rise as Supa phase 2 capacity ramps up.
Phase 2 expansion (+~16,000 MT, to ~59,000 MT installed) targeted by March 2027, with the next capacity wave in Q2 FY27.
Volume growth of ~26% (trailing 12 months) expected to be sustained through FY27 as phase 1 capacity is available for the full year.
Working capital target of 30-35 days, described as achievable over a multi-quarter process.
Export share target to return to historical peak of ~40% of revenue over time, not in the current year.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 43,445 MT at June 30, 2026, unchanged in Q1; 14,400 MT of the scheduled 30,000 MT expansion completed to date; target ~59,000 MT by March 2027.
Phase 2 project cost INR150-160 crore, partly funded from IPO proceeds; management said FY27 capex will be 'much higher than' INR50 crore, with a large part already incurred and some in advances.
Board authorised evaluation of ~10 acres of land in Supa MIDC for long-term expansion; management said it has not determined how many tons the land would add.
Existing Supa site has room for another ~10,000-12,000 MT without new land.
Peak insulated wires for EV traction motors are still being installed and are part of phase 2; not yet operational.
Management said CTC insulation lines are not fungible with standard or EV lines; only drawing capacity is shared. Further capacity additions will be triggered at ~85% utilisation.
demand_pricing: Hitachi Energy five-year framework agreement for winding wires to Indian and some global plants; quantity and price not yet defined. Products cover CTC, paper-insulated and enamel-insulated rectangular conductors; management said EBITDA per ton would be similar to the company average.
Some transformer OEMs in capacity expansion delayed picking up orders by a few weeks due to commissioning bottlenecks.
Pricing is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through; 80-85% of customers are on year-long value-addition contracts. New OEM customers were priced at higher, market-linked value-addition rates.
Management sees demand from T&D, data-centre-linked transformers and DG-set alternators, EV two- and three-wheelers, and passenger car/bus EV programmes contributing meaningfully around FY28-FY29.
BIS standards are shifting standard-wire supply toward Indian producers, per management.
LME copper has ranged roughly $10,000-14,000/MT recently (per management); value addition and realisation per ton include metal value.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA per ton so high in Q1, how sustainable is it, and has standard-wire EBITDA per ton improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to ~INR75,000/MT as the level it is comfortable delivering for FY27 (not formal guidance), with Supa Phase 2 adding higher fixed costs. Standard-wire EBITDA per ton improved marginally as round-wire utilisation rose; 765 kV was ~25% of CTC volume, and quantities were higher than prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there lumpiness in CTC orders, and will CTC revenue fall as standard capacity comes in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no lumpiness; CTC mix will revert toward normal as standard capacity arrives, but CTC absolute revenue and EBITDA are expected to grow. Management would not say EBITDA per ton rises for both segments.

qa_highlights.question: Hitachi Energy agreement: products, EBITDA per ton, and will more OEMs lock in supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Framework agreement only; quantity and price not yet defined. Products are CTC, paper-insulated and enamel-insulated rectangular conductors, with EBITDA per ton similar to the company average. Management said more OEMs are likely to lock in capacity given 3-4 year order books, with updates to come when finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Export share outlook and US/Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share was ~27% of operating revenue excluding other operating revenue in Q1; the target is to return to a historical peak of ~40% of revenue over time, not this year. Middle East, Europe and US are each 8-11% of total revenue annually; quarterly split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand cycle over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees T&D volumes rising, with OEMs holding 3-5 year order books and some capacity arriving in FY27 and some around 2029. Standard-wire demand from EV two/three-wheelers, AC compressors and DG-set alternators is strong, BIS is shifting supply to Indian producers, and passenger car/bus EV volumes are expected to be meaningful in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of INR93,000/MT EBITDA per ton and whether 75,000 can rise on higher-value products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three factors (mix, operating leverage, inventory) contributed but gave no quantified split. Dhruv Chopra said mix, led by record CTC contribution, was the main driver. Expectation is that higher specialized volumes help sustain or improve EBITDA per ton.

qa_highlights.question: Capex, land and capacity beyond 59,000 MT; can the same lines serve CTC and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 cost INR150-160 crore; FY27 capex to be well above INR50 crore. Land (~10 acres) is under evaluation with no tonnage estimate; the existing site has room for 10,000-12,000 MT. CTC insulation lines are not fungible with standard or EV lines, and further capacity is triggered around 85% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR17 crore interest cost, and what is the cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest reflects larger working-capital finance from higher turnover, not a rise in the cost of capital. Management said working-capital borrowing costs range from about 6% to 9.5%, depending on the instrument mix.

risks_watch: EBITDA per ton normalising toward the ~INR75,000 level as CTC mix reverts and Supa Phase 2 fixed costs rise; management says this is not formal guidance.
Phase 2 completion (~16,000 MT more, to ~59,000 MT installed) by March 2027, with the next capacity wave in Q2 FY27; slippage would delay volume growth.
Hitachi Energy framework agreement: quantity and price still undefined, so revenue and margin visibility remains limited.
Some transformer OEMs delaying order pick-up by a few weeks due to commissioning bottlenecks.
Export share at ~27% vs ~29% a year ago; the ~40% historical peak is a multi-period target, not this year.
Working capital at 60 days vs target of 30-35 days, described as a multi-quarter process; the Q1 interest cost rise shows the financing burden of growth.
Copper pass-through (LME roughly $10,000-14,000/MT) and FX drive reported revenue and margin; a weaker rupee has helped EBITDA per ton.

As yet, this is a framework agreement and the details are still being finalized.

summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, execution and the Hitachi framework, but cautious on forward EBITDA per ton, with repeated caveats that ~INR75,000 is not formal guidance. Management was evasive on specifics such as lumpiness, land tonnage, capacity timing beyond Q2 FY27, the Hitachi quantity and price, and the quantified split of EBITDA per ton.
